ai.promptTemplate: Build a workflow on the editor canvas for the following goal. Create each node with the addNode tool, using the available node types and a short descriptive label; addNode returns the id of the created node. Configure each node with what the goal asks for (prompt and model of an llm-chat, expression of a condition…), in the addNode config parameter or with configureNode, using only the config keys listed for that node type. Then connect the nodes in a logical order with connectNodes, using exactly the ids returned by addNode (never invent ids). To fix a node you created or a wrong edge, use removeNode/removeEdge instead of adding another node; do not remove nodes that were already in the flow unless the goal asks for it (the user will have to confirm). To classify and branch, use a decision node with provider llm (the platform LLM; without model it inherits the default) and a question whose ANSWER is the branch criterion (noul for yes/no, choice with the option), and branch on the answer with a condition or switch right after it, as in the examples of the branching rules in the context: the decision route measures the answer's confidence, it does not tell the category. A condition or switch expression reads the output of an earlier node by its id (${id.field}), never a bare word — fix an expression or config the tool refuses instead of leaving it behind. To put a node before an existing one, use addNode with insertBefore. When you are done, reply with a short summary of the flow. Goal: {{goal}}

fields.outputPassThroughHint: Output returns the input it received as the result. The fields below document the contract; the run does not validate them.
fields.nodeIdHint: The step output is stored under the id, not the name. Use in expressions:

fields.catalogOffline: Offline catalog — showing built-in components only

fields.noChatAdapterHint: This provider has no chat adapter on this server — the node will fail. Pick another one or the default.
fields.modelNotAllowedHint: This tenant does not allow this model — the run will fail. Pick one from the list.

fields.modelSearchHint: Type to search the catalog or to use another provider model id.
fields.userMessageHint: Empty: the previous step's output (after a Decision or Condition, the classification JSON). Use ${<Input node id>} for the run's original message; ${input} is the previous step's output. Objects go as JSON (for an API input like {"message": …}, use ${<Input node id>.message}); a reference with no value fails the step.
fields.knowledgeBaseHint: Searches the documents uploaded in Knowledge, in the workspace of whoever runs the flow, with the same embedding model used at ingestion. With a base selected, the vector backend is not used.
fields.knowledgeBaseMissing: The base stored in this node ({{value}}) does not exist in this workspace — the run will fail until you pick another one.
fields.knowledgeBaseLoadError: Could not list the knowledge bases.
fields.serverConnectionHint: Credentials and address live on the server, under {{value}}. The flow stores only the name.
fields.jdbcMemoryNotConnected: JDBC memory does not receive a DataSource in flows yet: the run fails. Use the redis backend.
fields.operationNotInPanel: Operation (operation — not in the panel yet)
fields.localModelPath: Local model path (local.model.path — not in the panel yet)
fields.localVocabPath: Local vocabulary path (local.vocab.path — not in the panel yet)
fields.memoryNeedsOperation: A Memory node made only in the designer cannot run yet: the engine requires the operation (add, get or clear) in "operation", and the panel does not have that field yet. Run stays blocked until the node has an operation.
fields.vectorStoreDoesNotWrite: This node does not store vectors yet: no vector backend has a write operation, and without "operation" (search, remove or removeAll) the engine refuses it. Run stays blocked. To search, use the Vector search node.
fields.localEmbeddingNotConfigurable: Local embedding requires the model and vocabulary paths (local.model.path, local.vocab.path), which the panel does not have yet: without them in the node the run fails and Run stays blocked. Use the OpenAI provider.
fields.approvalTitleHint: Name of the request in the Approvals queue.
fields.decisionRulesHint: Per question. choice: { "<question>": { "match": { "<option>": ["word", "re:regex"] }, "otherwise": "<option>" } }. score: keys are the level index and otherwise is a number, e.g. { "<question>": { "match": { "2": ["down"], "1": ["slow"] }, "otherwise": 0 } }. noul: { "<question>": { "matchAny": ["word", "re:regex"] } }. Without otherwise, no match is an error; falling into otherwise has confidence 0.
fields.decisionModelHint: Pin the version in production (e.g. typesafe/jev-1.13); an alias like ~typesafe/jev-latest can change on its own.
fields.decisionQuestionsHint: id → { type: choice | score | noul, instructions, criteria }. choice: option → description; score: ordered list of levels; noul: { true, false }.
fields.decisionStateHint: Template with ${path} placeholders resolved from the flow context. Empty: the node input.
fields.decisionGateHint: Comma-separated ids. Empty: all. The route uses the LOWEST confidence among them.
fields.thresholdHint: Below this → ESCALATE. Raise both for destructive actions.
fields.decisionOnErrorHint: ESCALATE: route ESCALATE with the reason (never a guess). FAIL: fail the step.
fields.decisionAcceptAt: Accept a cascade tier at confidence
fields.decisionCascadeHint: [{ provider, model }] tried in order when the previous tier answered with low confidence.
fields.decisionFallbacksHint: Tried only when a provider FAILS (down, no key, bad response).
fields.decisionConsensusHint: [{ provider, model }] vote on the same state; disagreement on the primary question lowers the route.
fields.decisionRoutesHint: An edge branch AUTO, REVIEW or ESCALATE follows the confidence of the answer, not the answer. To branch on what was answered, connect this node to a Condition or Switch that reads ${<id>.decision} or ${<id>.answers.<question>.result}.
fields.approvalDescriptionHint: Explain what the reviewer is deciding. The text is sent as is, with no variable substitution.
fields.proposalPayloadHint: What the reviewer assesses (and may edit before approving). Valid JSON becomes an object; other text is sent as is. Empty: the previous step's output.
fields.timeoutMinHint: When the deadline passes, the request is rejected. Empty: the server's global deadline (archflow.approval.timeout).
fields.onTimeoutAlwaysReject: Reject — always. An expired deadline means nobody looked, and that never becomes an approval.
fields.onTimeoutLegacy: This node has "{{value}}" saved as its on-timeout action. That option was removed and the engine ignores it: the expired request is rejected.
fields.conversationIdHint: Expression resolved against the execution context. Default uses conversationId from the upstream Linktor trigger.
fields.targetUserHint: Leave blank to return the conversation to the queue and let Linktor routing rules pick an agent.
fields.expressionHint: Boolean expression evaluated against the context. Use ${path.to.value} to reference upstream outputs.
fields.switchExpressionHint: Value compared against each case label.
fields.switchCasesHint: The keyword `default` matches anything unmatched by the other cases.
fields.itemVariableHint: Each iteration binds the current element under this name in the context.
fields.failFast: Fail fast if any branch errors
fields.outputVariableHint: Context path where the merged result is written.
fields.transformHint: Dialect: JSONata-style (current impl uses a simple ${path} + arithmetic/boolean evaluator).
fields.promptChunkHint: Static block of prompt. Combined with sibling chunks via their order.
fields.promptTemplateHint: Mustache-style template. Variables resolve against the flow context.
fields.requiredVariablesHint: Flow will fail-fast if any listed variable is missing at render time.
fields.jsonSchemaHint: If provided, validates the payload at the flow boundary.
fields.rejectIfMissing: Reject execution if input is missing
fields.argumentsHint: Passed as the tool's arguments object. Supports {{mustache}} against the flow context.
fields.inputMappingHint: Forwarded as the nested flow's input. Supports {{mustache}} substitution from the parent context.
fields.fireAndForget: Fire and forget (do not wait for completion)

config.subtitle: Connect the Linktor messaging platform so agents can talk on every channel.
config.connectionHint: Where Linktor lives and how to authenticate
config.enableHint: Exposes the Linktor MCP server to agents and the editor
config.mcpHint: The process archflow starts to talk to Linktor
config.title: Linktor
config.info: Linktor is an open-source omnichannel messaging platform (WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, SMS, Email, Webchat…). Once enabled, it shows up under MCP Servers and as a selectable server inside the workflow editor, giving agents direct access to ~51 Linktor tools (send message, list conversations, drive VRE visual responses, etc.).
config.baseUrlHint: Forwarded to the MCP server as LINKTOR_API_URL
config.apiKeyHint: LINKTOR_API_KEY. Leave masked placeholder to preserve.
config.mcpCommandHint: Command that starts the Linktor MCP server; space-separated args are supported. The executable (the first word) must be on the backend's MCP command allow-list.
config.saved: Configuration saved — it will be picked up on the next request.
config.installHint: npm install -g @linktor/mcp-server installs the linktor-mcp binary, but it is not on the default MCP command allow-list (which has launchers such as node and npx). Run node /path/to/linktor-mcp-server/dist/index.js, or allow the binary through the backend's ARCHFLOW_MCP_ALLOWED_COMMANDS variable (comma-separated; it replaces the default list, e.g. npx,node,linktor-mcp).
